chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: Armstrong and Joe Glaser: early pay
summary: Armstrong earned $750 a week at the Howard Theatre; he never heard him badly mention Glaser.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: What were people's impressions of people like Joe Glaser? You've mentioned something about it, I mean the fact that - oh, before I even do that (make a note of it) - do you know anything about the relationship between Louis Armstrong and Joe Glaser?
Yeah, I know they liked each other. I know he paid him. Louis Armstrong didn't make all that much money when he first started.
He didn't?
I know how much he made.
How much did he make?
He made $750 a week when I first started with him.
That was for the entire band, or for him?
For Louis Armstrong alone... in Washington, D. C.
What year was that?
That was the first year I played with him, because we played the Howard Theatre. I will never forget that. I thought he was making two or three thousand dollars.
You don't know what year that was, do you? Was that in the 30's?
The first year I was playing with him, whatever year it was. 1929
That was in the 30's.
We had chorus girls. You know we all traveled together in the bus.

That was after Louis Armstrong had come back from Europe. Did they ever talk about the contract Louis Armstrong was supposed to have signed with Joe Glaser for a certain sum of money for the rest of his life each week?
Never heard of it.

He talks about it - I mean he admits it but I was just wondering, I had heard that the figure was somewhere like $1000 or $1200 or something like that a week for the rest of his life - that he was supposed to have signed in 1932.
Well, it could have but I didn't know anything about it.
Louis Armstrong obviously never said anything bad about Joe Glaser.
I never heard him.
He never cussed him out, they didn't have a bad period when there was -
